claims.text: The starting material is an untreated CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix.
A tailored surface treatment will promote in situ formation of a stable, lubricious oxide tribofilm on CoCrFeNi.
The surface treatment will reduce friction relative to untreated CoCrFeNi throughout approximately 25–800 °C.
The surface treatment will reduce wear rate relative to untreated CoCrFeNi throughout approximately 25–800 °C.
The proposed intervention is a single optimized surface modification, exemplified by either controlled heat treatment or pre-oxidation.
The intervention is intended to form a nanocomposite tribolayer during sliding.
The resulting tribofilm will be continuous and self-adaptive.
The tribofilm will contain lubricious oxide phases likely enriched in Cr and/or other alloy components.
Oxygen exposure and mechanical stress during sliding will transform the pre-engineered surface layer into a thin, persistent oxide film.
The oxide film will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact.
Reduced metal-to-metal contact will lower the coefficient of friction.
Reduced metal-to-metal contact will lower the wear rate.
The expected wide-temperature stability of the film mirrors beneficial high-temperature behavior reported for other self-lubricating systems.
The anticipated improvement is bounded to controlled laboratory sliding under moderate loads in ambient air.
Extreme loads, non-ambient atmospheres, or prolonged cyclic thermal exposure may limit effectiveness or require treatment re-optimization.
